In this article, we'll walk you through the process of safely and efficiently disposing of your old appliance. **Assessing the Situation** Before you start removing your broken dishwasher, take a minute to assess the situation. Ask yourself a few questions: - Is the dishwasher still in working condition, but just not worth fixing? - Are there any hazardous materials or chemicals you need to be aware of when disposing of the appliance? - Do you have the necessary tools and equipment to safely remove and transport the dishwasher? This includes: - **Disconnecting the power**: Make sure the dishwasher is unplugged and the power is turned off at the circuit breaker or fuse box. - **Draining the water**: Empty any remaining water from the dishwasher's drain hose. - **Removing any doors or panels**: Take off any doors or panels to make it easier to load the dishwasher onto the removal truck. **Removing the Dishwasher** Once you've prepared the dishwasher, it's time to start removing it.
